item.title: Getting Sandbox Feedback without Greenlight?: Re: Getting Sandbox Feedback without Greenlight?
item.content:encoded:
Greenlights, while highly recommended for first-time authors, are only required to post in the Draft Critique Forum, and are obtained via concept threads in the Ideas Forum.

Additionally, another way of receiving critique is through the #thecritters chatroom on our IRC network (SkipIRC | irc.scpwiki.com | SSL Port: 6697), which while it doesn't require greenlights to get feedback there, some reviewers may refuse to look at drafts for new writers who haven't already gotten greenlights in the forums. If you want to head over there, make sure to read the Chat Guide I previously linked, and either way, I strongly recommend you go through the greenlight process in addition.

item.title: Need help with changing text in a similar way to offsets: Re: Need help with changing text in a similar way to offsets
item.content:encoded:
The definitive guide on ListPages stuff is ListPages Magic and You, which walks you through and explains how multi-iteration stuff works. In essence you make a couple hidden pages, then a main page with the ListPages, which pulls content from those hidden pages.

That guide semi-strongly advises using the order="created_at" parameter, but if you'd like it to be random you can change it to order="random". In order to get your reader to reload the page, you can provide a button somewhere that contains a link to the page itself; e.g. if you page is SCP-4260 then use [[[SCP-4260 | Refresh page?]]].

This will effectively mean that the contents of your reader sees will be random and cycle through randomly upon refreshing the page. If you have any further questions feel free to reach out.

Edit: Yes hello I am competent op staff who understands how reply nesting works

item.title: Can I start making tales or a related storyline? and how to make them?: Re: Can I start making tales or a related storyline? and how to make them?
item.content:encoded:
While waiting can start making tales or the storyline? Or should I wait for my SCP to be approved ?

If you're a first-time author, it's generally a good idea not to spend too much time drafting before you've gotten greenlights. You can start writing if you want to, but there's a chance you'll need to go back and rewrite your material if you don't have confirmation that reviewers like the basic idea.

And can I ask for advice how to make a storyline around my scp?

Sure, so long as you're not asking people to write the material for you.

item.title: Rewriting SCP concepts: Re: Rewriting SCP concepts
item.content:encoded:
do we just edit the original post or reply to the original post with the edited version?

Generally reviewers will look at the first post of a thread to critique a concept, so it's probably ideal to edit the original post. If you'd prefer to post a reply instead, you need to make it immediately clear to reviewers which post they should look at.

item.title: Help. I posted my SCP but it says access denied.: Re: Help. I posted my SCP but it says access denied.
item.content:encoded:
Alright, so what you have to do is go to the series page in question, and scroll to the bottom of the page. There, you should be able to see a series of red buttons; the furthermost one on the left being the word "edit". Click that, and scroll through the edit box to the slot № that you applied your article to ( * [[[SCP-5129]]] - [ACCESS DENIED] ).

Delete the text that says "[ACCESS DENIED]" and add whatever title you want. Do not change anything else on the page. Once finished, you can click save, and that's it. For the .aic elements like Secretary_Helen or CROM, it may take around 5 minutes to update, but Wikidot will do so instantly.
